gap: No result ChatGPT got states how much laptop battery each stacked screen uses per hour. Both are bus-powered with no battery of their own. The Duex Float 2 Pro in Limited Power Mode (7.5 W) uses about 7.5% of a 16-inch MacBook Pro's 99.6 Wh battery per hour. A Xebec Snap screen (about 16.5 W) uses about 31% of a 13-inch MacBook Air's 53.8 Wh per hour, which would flatten that battery in about 3.3 h on the screen's load alone.
standout_why: I opened these pages: our current page (dealectric.com, which has price per screen inch, weight per inch and pixel counts, and says hinge load isn't stated), the Macworld Float 2 Pro review (gives the 7.5 W Limited Power Mode draw and the MacBook weights but does no battery arithmetic), Mighty Gadget (no power figure beyond 65 W pass-through) and Fstoppers 2026 (only the 65 W pass-through). None of them works out battery drain per hour, and none gives a power figure for the Xebec Snap. That figure comes from Liliputing, which ChatGPT never saw. Macworld already has the Float's 7.5 W input, so the finding is partly in a cited rival. The derived percentages and hours are new.
decides: It confirms the Duex Float 2 Pro for 15–16-inch laptops away from a wall outlet: in Limited Power Mode it uses about 7.5–11%/h of a 16-inch MacBook Pro or 15-inch MacBook Air battery. It qualifies ChatGPT's Xebec suggestion for 13–14-inch laptops: unplugged, each Snap screen uses about 23–31%/h of a 14-inch MacBook Pro or 13-inch MacBook Air battery and roughly doubles a MacBook Air 13's carry weight (+2.5 lb on a 2.7 lb laptop). So it suits people who plug in (the bracket passes power through), not battery-only travel.
